info.description:
## Overview

Prototype Direct Integration API for managing appointments using FHIR R4 (4.0.1).

This specification contains the following operations:
* Search for appointments, including supported `_include` results.
* Get, create, update, patch and delete an appointment.
* Retrieve the server capability statement using `/metadata`.

## Relationship to BaRS

This prototype Direct Integration API is based on and aligned with the Booking and Referral Standard (BaRS). It focuses on the Appointment and metadata operations described in this specification.

BaRS is the definitive reference for the standard, including its requirements, resource definitions and implementation guidance. This prototype specification supplements that guidance for direct integration; it does not replace or redefine BaRS. If this specification differs from BaRS, the BaRS standard takes precedence, and the difference should be treated as a prototype limitation to be resolved.

Refer to the [BaRS implementation guide](https://simplifier.net/guide/nhsbookingandreferralstandard) for the authoritative guidance. Alignment with BaRS does not, by itself, establish that this prototype has been formally assessed or approved as conformant.

## Prototype configuration

The server URL is a placeholder. Replace it with the Direct Integration API deployment URL before use.

## Security and authentication

This prototype uses patient-based, user-restricted access through NHS login and NHS API Platform token exchange. This is the prototype's security profile; BaRS remains the definitive reference for the underlying standard.

### Authentication flow

Register the application separately with NHS login and NHS API Platform and enable access to this API in the chosen environment.

1. Authenticate the patient using the NHS login OpenID Connect authorisation-code flow and validate the returned ID token.
2. Exchange that ID token at the NHS API Platform token endpoint, authenticating the application with a signed client assertion.
3. Send the resulting API Platform access token as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on every API request, including `/metadata`.

Use `https://int.api.service.nhs.uk/oauth2/token` for integration testing and `https://api.service.nhs.uk/oauth2/token` for production. Follow the [NHS token-exchange guidance](https://digital.nhs.uk/developer/guides-and-documentation/security-and-authorisation/user-restricted-restful-apis-nhs-login-separate-authentication-and-authorisation) for request parameters, client assertions, token refresh and environment pairing.

The bearer credential for this API is the exchanged access token. Do not send an NHS login ID token, NHS login access token or client assertion as this API's bearer credential.

### Identity and verification

NHS login uses `openid` for authentication; request the approved `profile` scope when an NHS number is needed for patient matching. Validate identity claims and the returned verification level using the [NHS login OIDC guidance](https://nhsconnect.github.io/nhslogin/oidc-login-flow/) and [scopes and claims guidance](https://nhsconnect.github.io/nhslogin/scopes-and-claims/).

Prototype policy: appointment access requires high identity verification (P9). Configure the accepted authentication vectors during onboarding; do not infer adequate assurance merely from a successful sign-in. See [NHS login verification guidance](https://nhsconnect.github.io/nhslogin/step-up-p5-p9/).

### Patient authorisation — prototype policy

The API gateway must validate the API Platform access token and convey authenticated patient and application context to the receiving service through a trusted channel. A receiving service must reject caller-supplied identity context that has not been authenticated by that channel. Do not assume the access token is a locally decodable JWT.

Every appointment request must be authorised against the authenticated patient's local record:

* Searches return only that patient's appointments. Supplied identifiers and demographic filters must not broaden access to another patient.
* Reads, updates, patches and deletes require the appointment to belong to that patient.
* Creation must bind the appointment to that patient. Updates and patches must not reassign it to another patient.
* Included resources must be authorised for disclosure in the context of the permitted appointment.
* Acting for another patient requires a separately defined delegated-access policy; this prototype does not grant that access.

Authentication does not automatically permit every operation. The receiving service must also enforce its appointment-management rules and application permissions. Routing, software, organisation and practitioner headers provide context, not proof of patient identity.

### Authentication and authorisation failures

Return `401` for missing, invalid or expired API credentials, with a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` challenge. Return `403` when valid credentials lack sufficient permissions, patient access or required assurance. Return an OperationOutcome without disclosing another patient's details. OAuth token-endpoint errors follow the linked NHS guidance and are outside this API's paths.

### Prototype deployment

This specification defines the intended security contract. NHS login onboarding, API Platform product configuration, token validation and patient-level enforcement must be implemented and enabled before deployment. The placeholder API server URL does not imply that this prototype is already available on NHS API Platform.

## Errors

Error responses use HTTP status codes and the OperationOutcome structure defined in this specification.

searchParam.name: patient:identifier
searchParam.documentation:
The patient's NHS number. The primary identifier of a patient across systems, unique to NHS England and Wales. It can be used without reference to Name, Date of Birth or Postcode parameters.

|Type           |Expression|
|-------             | --------|
|[token](https://hl7.org/implement/standards/FHIR/search.html#token) |Appointment.participant.actor:identifier |

**Example query without encoding** 
*https://fhir.nhs.uk/Id/nhs-number|4857773456*

searchParam.name: patient:name
searchParam.documentation: The patient's name, including family, given, prefix, suffix and/or text. The Receiving system will check against any patient name fields they hold to establish a match. It is expected this parameter is used in conjunction with Date of Birth and Postcode to ensure a unique match.

searchParam.name: patient:birthdate
searchParam.documentation: The patient's Date of Birth. The Receiving system will check against the patient Date of Birth to establish a match. It is expected this parameter is used in conjunction with Name and Postcode to ensure a unique match.

searchParam.name: patient:address-postalcode
searchParam.documentation: The patient's Home address Postcode. The Receiving system will check against the patient 'Home' address Postcode to establish a match. It is expected this parameter is used in conjunction with Name and Date of Birth to ensure a unique match.

get.description:
### Returns bookings for a specified patient
Use this endpoint to get all bookings for a given patient. All bookings for the specified patient at the specified target endpoint will be returned in a FHIR searchset Bundle containing Appointment resources. 

If a sender wants to cancel a particular booking, they must perform a read first, comparing and amending the details prior to performing the update.

Patient access: the receiving service must authorise this operation for the authenticated patient and restrict all returned or modified resources accordingly. See the patient-authorisation policy in the API overview.

BookingsForPatient.description: A default response, with no `_include` parameters supplied, containing only the matched Appointment resources.

BookingsForPatientWithIncludes.summary: Get bookings for a patient, with _include=Appointment:slot&_include=Slot:schedule&_include=Schedule:actor:HealthcareService&_include=HealthcareService:location
BookingsForPatientWithIncludes.description:
A response to a request such as:

`GET [base]/Appointment?patient:identifier=https://fhir.nhs.uk/Id/nhs-number|4857773456&_include=Appointment:slot&_include=Slot:schedule&_include=Schedule:actor:HealthcareService&_include=HealthcareService:location`

The matched Appointment is returned with `search.mode: "match"`, and each additionally requested resource (Slot, Schedule, HealthcareService and Location) is returned alongside it in the same Bundle with `search.mode: "include"`, so the sender does not need to make separate follow-up reads to resolve them.

PatientId_QParam.name: patient:identifier
PatientId_QParam.description:
The patient's NHS number. The primary identifier of a patient across systems, unique to NHS England and Wales. It can be used without reference to Name, Date of Birth or Postcode parameters.

|Type           |Expression|
|-------             | --------|
|[token](https://hl7.org/implement/standards/FHIR/search.html#token) |Appointment.participant.actor:identifier |

**Example query without encoding** 
*https://fhir.nhs.uk/Id/nhs-number|4857773456*


For patient access, the supplied NHS number must match the authenticated patient. If omitted, the server must still restrict the search to that patient.

AppointmentInclude_QParam.name: _include
AppointmentInclude_QParam.description:
Inclusions that drive the recursive depth of the search. Use this to ask the Receiver to return additional resources referenced by the Appointment(s), in the same response Bundle, rather than the sender having to perform separate follow-up reads.

**Note**: _include shares the same syntax as _revinclude - up to three components, separated by colon characters (:). Unlike search queries, this is not a FHIRPath expression.

The parameter can be repeated to request more than one inclusion on the same request, allowing a full chain of related resources (for example Appointment -> Slot -> Schedule -> HealthcareService -> Location) to be resolved in a single call.

The full list of applicable _includes are shown below. If any cannot be honoured the Receiver will respond, ignoring the unsupported _include(s), with the url reflecting this omission in the response Bundle.link.url.

|Expression                        | Inclusion         |Description|
|-------                           |--------           |-------- |
| Appointment:slot                 | Slot               | Include the Slot Resource(s) referenced within the Appointment Resources|
| Appointment:based-on             | ServiceRequest     | Include the ServiceRequest (referral) Resource that the Appointment is based on|
| Slot:schedule                    | Schedule           | Include Schedule Resources referenced within the Slot Resources|
| Schedule:actor:Practitioner      | Practitioner       | Include Practitioner Resources referenced within the Schedule Resources|
| Schedule:actor:PractitionerRole  | PractitionerRole   | Include PractitionerRole Resources referenced within the Schedule Resources|
| Schedule:actor:HealthcareService | HealthcareService  | Include HealthcareService Resources referenced within the Schedule Resources|
| HealthcareService:providedBy     | Organization       | Include Organization Resources referenced within the HealthcareService Resources|
| HealthcareService:location       | Location           | Include Location Resources referenced within the HealthcareService Resources|

**Example usage**

Get bookings for a patient and include just the Slot each booking is linked to:

`GET [base]/Appointment?patient:identifier=https://fhir.nhs.uk/Id/nhs-number|4857773456&_include=Appointment:slot`

Get bookings for a patient and resolve the chain from Slot through to the HealthcareService and Location it is delivered at:

`GET [base]/Appointment?patient:identifier=https://fhir.nhs.uk/Id/nhs-number|4857773456&_include=Appointment:slot&_include=Slot:schedule&_include=Schedule:actor:HealthcareService&_include=HealthcareService:location`

Get bookings for a patient and include the referral (ServiceRequest) each booking was based on:

`GET [base]/Appointment?patient:identifier=https://fhir.nhs.uk/Id/nhs-number|4857773456&_include=Appointment:based-on`

RequestingOrganisation.title: NHSD-End-User-Organisation
RequestingOrganisation.description:
Requesting Organization described in an object based on a FHIR 'Organization' resource (Standard Base64 encoded JSON).
This header is optional in the API definition because its use depends on the authentication mode. It MUST be provided for application-based authentication and SHOULD NOT be provided for patient-based authentication. It does not identify the patient and must not be used to establish patient authorisation.

In this example an ODS code and the Organisation name is provided. Other identifiers are permitted if required.

RequestingPractitioner.title: NHSD-Requesting-Practitioner
RequestingPractitioner.description:
Requesting Practitioner described in an object based on a FHIR 'PractitionerRole' resource (Standard Base64 encoded JSON).

This item is not mandatory, however if the information is available it must be included in the request. Only in the event that it is not available, should it be omitted.

The example below shows a General Practitioner and their SDS Role profile Id.
The Base64 encoded example below shows a General Practitioner and their SDS Role profile Id.

RequestingSoftware.title: NHSD-Requesting-software
RequestingSoftware.description:
Requesting Software described in an object based on a FHIR 'Device' resource (Standard Base64 encoded JSON).
Access-control requirements for these headers depend on the receiving implementation. 

The identifier used here, though arbitrary, should be consistent across instances of a product, the name and version of the product should also be accurate and consistent.

NHSLoginPatientAccess.description: NHS API Platform access token obtained after NHS login authentication and token exchange. Applies to all operations. See Security and authentication in the API overview. OpenAPI 3.0 has no native token-exchange flow, so this scheme describes the bearer credential presented to this API.
